title: RocksDB — Derived System Card (code-to-spec)
source: facebook/rocksdb @ c9252b9 (v11.5.0). Embedded persistent LSM storage engine, C++.
purpose: An embeddable, persistent, ordered key-value store optimized for fast storage (flash/SSD). Linked into a host process as a library; the host owns any networking/sharding/replication.

operations: column families (independent keyspaces sharing one WAL)
interface.semantics: Keys and values are opaque byte strings (Slice). Keys are ordered by a comparator (default bytewise); range scans supported. Internally each key carries a 56-bit sequence number + value type.
interface.access_pattern: Point ops + ordered range scans; Merge operands for read-time aggregation.

data_model.property: Internal key = user key + 56-bit sequence + 8-bit type; values opaque
data_model.guarantee: Multiple versions of a key coexist (MVCC); deletions are tombstones. Memtable = skiplist; SST = block-based (data+index+bloom+footer).

durability.property: WAL + flush + MANIFEST; fsync tunable per write
durability.guarantee: WriteOptions::sync=true => fsync per write, 0 loss; sync=false => OS-buffered, lost on power loss. Flush turns memtable into durable SSTs; MANIFEST records the live file set atomically (temp+rename+dir fsync). Recovery = read CURRENT→MANIFEST, replay WAL.
durability.evidence: db/log_writer.cc:87 AddRecord; include/rocksdb/options.h WriteOptions::sync; db/flush_job.cc FlushJob::Run; db/version_set.cc LogAndApply; db/db_impl/db_impl_open.cc Recover

consistency.property: Single-process MVCC via monotonic sequence numbers; snapshot isolation
consistency.guarantee: A read sees writes with seq ≤ its snapshot. Snapshots pin a sequence and hold back compaction GC. WriteBatch is atomic at one sequence point. NOT distributed — WAL-tailing (GetUpdatesSince) lets an external layer build replication.
consistency.evidence: db/dbformat.h sequence numbers; include/rocksdb/snapshot.h + db/snapshot_impl.h; db/write_batch.cc; include/rocksdb/transaction_log.h GetUpdatesSince

space_reclamation.property: Compaction is the GC; block cache bounds read memory
space_reclamation.guarantee: Compaction merges overlapping SSTs and drops overwritten keys + tombstones (only when below the oldest live snapshot). Leveled (default, low space amp / high write amp), universal, or FIFO. Block cache (LRU/clock) caps read-side RAM; memtable flush frees write-side RAM; write stalls when L0/compaction falls behind.
space_reclamation.evidence: db/compaction/compaction_job.cc CompactionJob::Run; db/compaction/compaction_iterator.cc (drop by earliest_snapshot); cache/lru_cache.cc, cache/clock_cache.cc; db/column_family.cc RecalculateWriteStallConditions

concurrency.property: Multi-threaded: group-commit writes + concurrent skiplist + background pools
concurrency.guarantee: Many threads call Get/Put concurrently. A write leader serializes the WAL append for a batch group; followers insert into the concurrent skiplist in parallel. Flush/compaction run on background thread pools. A short-held DB mutex protects VersionSet metadata; reads are lock-free via SuperVersion ref-counting. Scales across cores (vs Redis single thread).
concurrency.evidence: db/write_thread.cc JoinBatchGroup/EnterAsBatchGroupLeader; memtable/inlineskiplist.h InsertConcurrently; util/threadpool_imp.cc; db/db_impl/db_impl.h mutex_; db/column_family.h SuperVersion Ref/Unref

partitioning.property: Column families (logical, single node); no built-in sharding
partitioning.guarantee: Each column family is an independent LSM tree (own memtables/SSTs/options) sharing one WAL and process; a WriteBatch can atomically span CFs. L1+ SSTs are non-overlapping key ranges. No cross-machine distribution — sharding/replication is the embedder's job (MyRocks, TiKV, CockroachDB). OpenAsSecondary gives a read-only file-tailing replica.
partitioning.evidence: db/column_family.cc ColumnFamilyData/ColumnFamilySet; include/rocksdb/db.h CreateColumnFamily; db/db_impl/db_impl_secondary.cc OpenAsSecondary

transactions.property: Real ACID transactions with rollback (pessimistic 2PL or optimistic)
transactions.guarantee: WriteBatch alone = atomic, not isolated. TransactionDB adds isolation + rollback: Pessimistic takes key locks (GetForUpdate), conflicts block/time-out; Optimistic detects conflicts at commit via sequence numbers and fails (retry). Uncommitted writes live in a WriteBatchWithIndex and never touch the DB until commit, so rollback is free. STRICTLY stronger than Redis's no-rollback MULTI/EXEC.

design_space_notes: RocksDB's defining choices vs a from-scratch builder: LSM (write-optimized, persistent, larger-than-memory) vs in-memory; compaction style (leveled=low space amp/high write amp, universal=opposite, FIFO=expiry); multi-threaded group commit vs single thread; real ACID vs no-rollback; single-node library vs distributed.
